name: Flowponent
tagline: 1,091 copy-paste Webflow cloneable sections, 335 of them free
description: Flowponent is a searchable library of Webflow cloneable UI components — mostly whole page sections you copy to the clipboard and paste straight into the Webflow Designer. The homepage reports 1,091 components split into 756 Pro and 335 Free, tagged by section type and layout. It is aimed at Webflow designers assembling marketing sites fast, and the same team also runs Figma, Tailwind and stock-photo side products.
agent_guidance: Only reach for this when the target is a Webflow project — the output is Webflow clipboard JSON, not HTML or JSX, so it is worthless in a React or Tailwind codebase. Use the tag facets (hero, footer, pricing, checkout, 2-columns) to narrow before browsing, and expect to hit the Pro paywall on roughly 70 percent of results. You cannot scrape it: /components and /pricing render as an empty Nuxt shell, and /llms.txt returns the SPA fallback rather than a real index.
why_it_matters: One of the larger curated Webflow cloneable catalogues, with a genuinely usable free tier of 335 sections — but it is locked to one no-code platform and gives an agent nothing to read.

name: Material Design 3
tagline: Google's open design system: 39 components, tokens, and Compose/Web code
description: Material Design 3 is Google's official design system documentation — foundations, styles (colour, typography, elevation, motion, icons), design tokens, and per-component specification pages. The sitemap lists 375 pages, of which 39 are components, plus implementation guides for Jetpack Compose, MDC-Android, Flutter and the Web. It is the canonical reference for anyone building Android UI or matching Google's visual language, and the M3 Expressive update is documented alongside it.
agent_guidance: Treat this as the spec, not the source — m3.material.io is a client-rendered Angular app that returns only 'This website requires JavaScript' to any fetcher, so read https://m3.material.io/sitemap.xml to enumerate pages and then pull the actual API surface from the Compose or material-web source instead. Reach for M3 over a generic web system whenever the target is Android or a Google-adjacent product, especially for dynamic colour and the design-token naming; do not use it for a Tailwind or shadcn app, where the token model will fight you. Note the vocabulary drift: M3 calls a bottom tab bar a 'navigation bar' and a snackbar a toast.
why_it_matters: The most complete free design system on the web, and the only one that ships colour theory, motion specs, tokens, and shipping code for three platforms at once.
notable_for: Jetpack Compose, MDC-Android, Flutter and Web guides
evidence: WebFetch https://m3.material.io/ and https://m3.material.io/components (both returned title only — JS shell), curl https://m3.material.io/components (200, body is 'This website requires JavaScript'), curl + parse https://m3.material.io/sitemap.xml (375 URLs; 39 component slugs; top sections foundations/styles/components/develop/blog/m3-expressive), WebFetch https://m3.material.io/develop (title: 'Develop with Material Design 3 for Android & Web'), curl https://m3.material.io/llms.txt (404)

name: Grids by Obys
tagline: Scroll-driven microsite by Obys Agency teaching layout grid systems
description: Grids is an educational microsite from the Ukrainian studio Obys Agency about the grid systems they use in everyday layout work, told through scroll-driven animation. It is built and hosted on Readymag and is a desktop-first experience — the only text the raw HTML exposes is 'Rotate your device for the best experience' and 'And wait a few seconds.' The lesson content itself is rendered entirely in JavaScript, so it can only be consumed by a human in a browser.
agent_guidance: Send a human here for grid intuition and motion craft; do not try to read it yourself — the page is a Readymag export whose entire body is a JS payload, so a fetch returns nothing but a rotate-your-device prompt. If you need citable, quotable grid theory for a spec or a DESIGN.md, use Müller-Brockmann's system or a text-based source instead, and keep this link purely as inspiration for the art direction. It also renders badly on mobile by its own admission.
why_it_matters: A well-regarded piece of studio-made design education, and a good example of a scroll narrative — but it is an experience, not a resource an agent or a search index can use.
notable_for: grid systems taught through scroll storytelling

name: Tremor
tagline: 40 copy-paste React chart and dashboard components, plus 300+ free blocks
description: Tremor is a React component library for charts and dashboards built on Tailwind CSS, Radix UI and Recharts, distributed as copy-paste source rather than a black-box package. The docs list 40 components across visualizations, inputs and UI, and blocks.tremor.so adds 300+ blocks in 27 categories plus 6 full Next.js templates — all now free and open source. Tremor Labs is joining Vercel, and the templates ship as GitHub repos with one-click Vercel deploy. Best suited to teams building analytics surfaces, internal tools or SaaS dashboards in Next.js.

templates.name: Planner
templates.purpose: Dashboard template for a SaaS or internal tool: advanced tables, interactive charts, custom tooltips. Next.js 15, React 19, Tailwind v3.4.

templates.name: Solar
templates.purpose: One-page SaaS marketing website with hero, feature, header and CTA sections and animated SVG illustrations. Next.js 15, Tailwind v4, Motion v12.

templates.name: Overview
templates.purpose: Four dashboard overview pages — KPI overview, retention chart, scenario analysis, notifications panel. Next.js 15 with TanStack Table and Recharts.

templates.name: Insights
templates.purpose: Data-application template for feeding and tracking data, including user onboarding flows.

templates.name: Dashboard
templates.purpose: Simple dashboard template for presenting data with minimal chrome.

templates.name: Database
templates.purpose: Website template for a database or data-infrastructure product.

pricing_detail: Free. Blocks and templates were previously paid and are now free and open source; every template is a public GitHub repo with a .zip download and a Deploy-to-Vercel link.
agent_guidance: Prefer Tremor over hand-rolling Recharts when the brief is an analytics or internal dashboard and the project is already Next.js plus Tailwind — the KPI cards, tracker and chart-tooltip blocks are the real time-saver, not the buttons. It is not a shadcn registry: there is no `add` command, you copy the component file in and install the peer Radix packages yourself, so budget for the long dependency install listed in the Next.js guide. Watch the version drift — the open-source repo's last push was October 2025 and Tremor Labs is folding into Vercel, so pin your Tailwind and Recharts versions and expect to maintain the copied files yourself.
why_it_matters: The clearest chart-component vocabulary in the React ecosystem, and the paid blocks and templates going free and open source made it one of the best-value dashboard kits available.
notable_for: 6 open-source Next.js templates with Vercel deploy

name: Chakra UI
tagline: 114 accessible React components with a token-driven styling system
description: Chakra UI is a React component system built on Ark UI and Zag.js state machines, with a token-based styling engine and first-class dark mode. Version 3.36.1 documents around 114 components across layout, typography, forms, collections, overlays, feedback and data display, installed as an npm package and scaffolded with a CLI snippet command. It ships an official MCP server and llms.txt files, so agents can query components and theme tokens directly. Chakra UI Pro adds paid pre-built pages and templates.
pricing_detail: Core library is free and MIT. Chakra UI Pro (pro.chakra-ui.com) sells pre-built application, marketing and e-commerce pages; a Pro licence also unlocks the list_component_templates and get_component_templates MCP tools. Exact Pro prices were not shown on the pages fetched.
agent_guidance: Reach for Chakra instead of shadcn/ui when the team wants a versioned dependency they can upgrade rather than owned source files they must maintain, and when they need breadth — date picker, colour picker, splitter, rich text editor and tree view all exist here and do not in a stock shadcn install. Always run `npx @chakra-ui/cli snippet add` after installing: v3 splits primitives from the composed snippets, and code written against v2's prop API will not compile. Best of all, add the MCP server with `claude mcp add chakra-ui -- npx -y @chakra-ui/react-mcp` and call list_components and get_component_props rather than guessing — and use the v2_to_v3_code_review tool on any legacy Chakra codebase before touching it.
why_it_matters: One of the few large React libraries that is simultaneously accessibility-serious, actively shipping, and genuinely agent-legible — llms.txt, an official MCP server, and 40k stars behind it.
notable_for: built on Ark UI and Zag.js state machines
